# This file is generated to mirror docs/COMMANDS.org (the Emacs-client
# command reference), translated to Neovim keybindings and :Skg*
# Ex commands. nvim/lua/skg/keymaps.lua is the authoritative skgrepo
# for every binding named here; if this file and that module disagree,
# keymaps.lua wins. Where COMMANDS.org describes Emacs-only mechanics
# (the minibuffer, magit), the text below is rewritten for the nvim
# equivalents (vim command-line prompts, neogit / plain git-diff
# buffers) rather than translated word for word.
* user-facing skg commands
** :w : :SkgSave
Each time you save, your view is rebuilt.
This is because you can put 'requests' into your view,
in which you request more data,
such as a node's ancestors, or the nodes that link to it.
Since views can overlap,
saving one open view can change another.
You may edit several views at once, but Neovim asks when an edit
first dirties a view while another view already has unsaved edits;
choosing Cancel restores the view's last clean text. On save, Skg checks the other dirty
views' last clean text and current text against every graph identity the
prepared save can affect. A conflict is a hard refusal before any write;
the error names the views and IDs. Missing or malformed baseline data is
also refused conservatively. There is no "save anyway" choice.

':w' is the BufWriteCmd on every skg view buffer, so plain saving
works as expected; ':SkgSave' does the same thing as an explicit
Ex command.

If the current files for anything being saved select a title or body
from below that node's home, Skg stops before every write and offers
*Hoist* or *Abort*. Hoist moves the selected text to home, removes
lower title/body copies, and preserves lower relationships and aliases;
the exact approved PIDs are reread and rechecked as one batch before the
save proceeds. Abort leaves every file byte-for-byte unchanged. Scripts
and maintenance writers have no prompt and refuse this repair.

That disk-publication choice is separate from displaying the result. If
a successful save under a restricted skgrepo-set would rerender text from
an overPrivateText telescope, Skg asks for a second, request-scoped approval. Decline
leaves the save skgsave-committed but sends no new view text and changes no
open-view registry entry.
** :SkgShowUnsavedChanges : archive edits for manual recovery
Prompts for a local Org file, writes a detached recovery document, opens
it, and reports its actual path. The document contains context, lossless
JSON strings for the clean baseline and current text, and a readable
unified diff. It does not save graph data, close or clean the source view,
or register the archive as a live view.

When a save is refused, archive the relevant dirty views, close those live
views, save the remaining view, reopen fresh views, and manually reapply
the intended edits. Do not save an entire stale archived copy over the
newer graph. If dirty search results were enriched, the archive labels that
the diff also includes enrichment presentation and is not a semantic patch
of user intent alone.
** <localleader>dd : deletion
***     <localleader>dd : :SkgDelete
Marks the node at point for deletion from the graph.
Upon saving the view, it will vanish not just from this view,
but from the graph itself.
*** <localleader>dR : :SkgDeleteRecursive
Same as Delete, but also marks every unrestrictedNode viewdescendant
of the node at point. Descendent headlines that are not unrestrictedNodes
(phantoms, aliasFolder, id-folder, etc.) are skipped.

Its own binding, not a prefix-arg variant -- nvim has no prefix-arg
protocol to reuse here the way Emacs's C-u did. Call it directly as
<localleader>dR, or as ':SkgDeleteRecursive'.
*** <localleader>da : :SkgDeleteReferencesToAbsentNode
On an Unknown phantom, remove that exact raw ID from owned structured
relationships throughout retained telescopes, then refresh only views which
show a changed recorder or that exact raw ID.
The command refuses while a view is dirty.  Text links are reported but left
unchanged, and require confirmation before the structural cleanup.  If the
scan changes before confirmation, the command refuses the stale approval;
run it again to rescan.  The warning ends by naming the Emacs command
skg-investigate-unknown-node, whose twin here is <localleader>tr.
** <localleader>f : text search
The 'f' is for 'find'.
*** <localleader>ff : :SkgSearch
Text search across titles and aliases, returning every
matching node. Prominent nodes (roots, cycle members,
mentioned nodes, and nodes that had an org-roam ID before import)
are bumped in the ranking via their prominence multiplier.

A node with =NoSearchMatching= cannot be a direct title, alias, or body hit
in any search mode. It may still appear as context for another hit and remains
openable by ID. This is decluttering, not privacy. A packing list mentioning
“shaver,” for example, can be excluded while the shaver node still matches.

Prompts for search terms. All search axes take their conservative
defaults: no per-token regex, titles only (no body), no Tantivy
phrase and operator syntax.

Under a restricted skgrepo-set, if the search index contains any overPrivateText
telescope (one whose selected title or body lies below home), Skg asks
whether to include or exclude overPrivateText telescopes before running the query.
Exclude filters them in Tantivy before matching; Include is permission
for this search only. Under skgrepo-set =all= they are included without a
prompt and the result carries a warning.

Run 'Goto' (<localleader>gg, below) from one of the links in the
search results to open the view from that node.
*** <localleader>fi : :SkgSearchInteractive (search-interactive)
Same as Search, but after the search terms it prompts:

: Type a character for each search option: (r)egex, (b)ody, (t)antivy syntax, (h)elp:

Type one character for each option you want, in any order,
then press Enter. An empty answer uses the same conservative
defaults as ':SkgSearch'. Unrecognized characters are ignored.
Typing =h= opens this documentation (docs/COMMANDS-nvim.org,
falling back to docs/COMMANDS.org if that file is missing), with
all folds opened and the cursor searched onto this headline -- and
abandons the search. If the headline can't be found the whole file
is still shown, with a notice that the search failed.

- =r= (*regex*) — per-token regex instead of phrase search.
  Bypasses the query parser; each whitespace-separated piece
  is handed to Tantivy's 'RegexQuery'.
- =b= (*body*) — also search the body field (titles are
  always searched).
- =t= (*tantivy syntax*) — Tantivy phrase and operator syntax
  (AND/OR/NOT/+/-). In non-regex mode this passes through
  Tantivy's QueryParser (phrase quotes, grouping, field: all
  work; intra-word operator chars get escaped so =foo:bar=
  remains findable). In regex mode, AND / OR / NOT / +foo /
  -bar combine the per-piece RegexQueries at the document
  level; phrase syntax does not apply there. See the regex=true
  section below.
**** Query syntax with default axes (phrase/operators=false, regex=false)
Queries are literal. The query string is split on whitespace,
and any word containing a Tantivy operator character
(=+ - & | ! ( ) { } [ ] ^ " ~ * ? : \=) or the bare keyword
=AND= / =OR= / =NOT= is wrapped as a phrase so its contents
are searched literally. Words without specials pass through.
- *OR between words*. "dog cat" matches titles containing
  either word; a title with both outranks one with only one.
- *Literal special characters*. A title like "C++ tips",
  "[draft] plan", or "cat:dog" is findable by typing its
  literal text.
**** Query syntax with phrase/operators=true
The query is handed to Tantivy's QueryParser, with one
heuristic adjustment: any operator character sitting strictly
inside a word (with word chars on both sides, scanning
through consecutive operators within the same token) is
backslash-escaped. So =foo:bar= stays findable as a literal,
but =AND= / =OR= / =+foo= / =-bar= / ="fox in socks"= /
=(dog OR cat)= keep their operator meaning.

Known imperfection: the heuristic can't distinguish a
configured field name from a user word, so
=title_or_alias:dog= gets its =:= escaped too. Field-
qualified queries need manual =\:= in operators mode.
**** Query syntax with regex=true
The query is split on whitespace and each piece is handed to
'tantivy::query::RegexQuery' as its own pattern. Matches are
against *tokens*, not raw text: the indexer lowercases and
splits on whitespace, so no stored token ever contains a
space. That's why splitting is the only way multi-word regex
queries return anything. Patterns like =histor.*= work for
prefix search ('history', 'historical'), and =polit.* scien.*=
combines two such prefix searches. Combine with body=true to
also search body fields.

The *=*= gotcha*: in regex =*= means "zero or more of the
previous character", not "any characters" (that's =.*=). So
=sci*= matches the tokens =sc=, =sci=, =scii=, … — not
"anything starting with sci". Use =sci.*= for that.

With operators=false, pieces are OR'd (SHOULD-combined)
like the non-regex default.

With phrase/operators=true (the wire flag is still
=operators=true=), the keywords =AND= / =OR= / =NOT= and the
prefixes =+piece= / =-piece= combine the per-piece RegexQueries
at the document level:
- =poli.* AND sci.*= — documents whose tokens include one
  matching =poli.*= and one matching =sci.*=.
- =poli.* NOT bio.*= — documents matching =poli.*= and not
  any token matching =bio.*=.
- =+poli.* -bio.*= — same as above, without the keywords.
- =poli.* OR sci.*= — explicit OR, same as the default.
Keywords are consumed rather than matched as patterns. An
=AND= adjacent to a piece on either side promotes that piece
to MUST.
**** Caveats
- Each alias is indexed as its own document, so a query can
  match on an alias even when the title doesn't mention the
  searched word. The returned node is still the aliased one.
- Results are ranked by BM25 times a prominence multiplier
  (Root 100×, CycleMember ~32×, Mentioned 10×, HadID 10×,
  MultiContained ~3.2×, everything else 1×). A weaker text
  match on a root can outrank a stronger match on a leaf,
  but every match is returned — search is never filtered by
  graph role.
- Regex distance is tokenwise: a pattern never spans
  whitespace, because we split the query on whitespace before
  handing the pieces to RegexQuery. A true whole-title regex
  (one pattern that matches across spaces) would need a
  separate non-tokenized =raw_title= field. Not done yet.
*** <localleader>fl : :SkgSearchMakeLink
Search-then-link: pick a result, return here, get a link.

Like ':SkgSearch' but tailored for inserting a link to a node
you don't yet know the ID of. The buffer and cursor position you
called it from are remembered. The same conservative search
defaults as ':SkgSearch' apply.

Unlike the Emacs client, the source buffer is not saved before
the search runs -- only its position is recorded. (Saving first
can let the server's rerender collapse a freshly typed blank
line, leaving the remembered position dangling on the next
headline, so the inserted link would glue itself to the wrong
spot.) Save your own edits first if you want them preserved
before detouring into the search.

In the resulting search buffer, find the result you want and
press <CR> (or <localleader>cc). The search buffer closes; you
return to the buffer you started in, at the position you were at;
and a =[[id:X][LABEL]]= link is inserted at point.

The label is the result's title with any inline links inside
it reduced to their labels (so the new link's label is plain
text, never another link inside a link).
** <localleader>g : going to a node
*** <localleader>gg : :SkgGoto
Calling this when the cursor is on a link, a node's metadata,
a bare UUID, or a .skg filename
will open a new view from the ID it finds there,
or go to the view of it that was already open if that exists.

The requested node itself is always the raw root. Recursive content
below it can still use override substitution. Override facts remain
visible in enriched search results and through the override folder
and role-tree commands.

If you're not sure whether the cursor is on something visitable
(a link or a node's metadata),
use IdNext and IdPrev (the ]i / [i motions, or <localleader>in /
<localleader>ip)
to identify where those are.
*** <localleader>GG : :SkgGotoAndCloseThis
Like Goto, but also closes the buffer it was called from.
*** <localleader>gb : :SkgGotoBiggestBranch
Go to the branch near point with the most recursive content,
estimated by counting viewdescendants in the current buffer.

If the node at point has siblings, this considers that sibling
set. If it has no siblings, it considers the node's immediate
children instead.

This can help when a view is loading slowly:
replacing the content relationship to its biggest branch
with a link relationship (<localleader>ml)
reduces the view's demands on the server.
*** <localleader>gi : :SkgGotoById
'Goto' is usually more convenient.

This requires a literal v4 UUID string, like
3861db2c-7f16-4814-b403-52b5e05d5e0a
It can be useful going from git to skg.
*** <localleader>Gi : :SkgGotoByIdAndCloseThis
*** <localleader>gm : :SkgGotoInGit
Opens a neogit status view of the changes to the file containing
the node at point. If the file appears in multiple sections
(unstaged, staged, untracked), point lands on the first and
the user is warned. (If neogit is unavailable, this falls back
to the plain git-diff view described below.)
*** <localleader>Gm : :SkgGotoInGitAndCloseThis
*** <localleader>gM : :SkgGotoInGitParent
Opens a plain git-diff buffer (named =skg://git-diff/FILE=) of
the *parent*'s file -- the combined staged+unstaged diff, or the
untracked file's own content if it has no HEAD diff -- with point
on the first line in that buffer containing this node's ID.
Warns if the ID appears multiple times. (Emacs's magit has an API
for landing on a specific line within a status section; neogit
doesn't, so this variant uses a plain diff buffer instead of a
neogit view -- same information, different chrome.)
*** <localleader>GM : :SkgGotoInGitParentAndCloseThis
** <localleader>t : git operations
*** <localleader> (g|G)(m|M) : :SkgGotoInGit*
These four commands are described elsewhere in this document.
*** <localleader>tr         : :SkgInvestigateUnknownNode
The twin of Emacs's skg-investigate-unknown-node. Says what an
unknown node is: a reference that no node answers to, shown as
"Reference to unknown node.". On such a headline it takes that ID;
anywhere else it asks for one. The answer opens read-only in
=skg://unknown-node=, as Org text. If the ID resolves to a node, it
names that node, its ID and its home skgrepo. Otherwise it searches
the git history (first parents, from HEAD) of every skgrepo, and
reports the most recent commit that held the ID's file, the commit it
vanished at, its title then, its own relation lists then, and every
node that referred to it then, links included; or that the ID was
never in any skgrepo's history. If HEAD still holds the ID's file,
it says so: "still present at HEAD (only the worktree lacks it)". It
refuses unless the skgrepo restriction is 'all'; a refusal opens the
same buffer, as "* investigation failed" with the reason under it.
** <localleader>l : show a folder (both folders of a relation)
These commands don't edit the graph. Each inserts a request into the
metadata of the node at point that, on save, causes the server to
render the relation's folder viewnodes into the view, populated from
the graph. Each builds both folders of its relation (but containers and
mentioners build one). The write-protected folder ☮
marks a folder you cannot change from here. Every command auto-saves.
Without such a request, an editable node shows only its nonempty
subscribeeFolder (plus the nonempty hiddenInSubscribeeFolder on an editable
subscribee-as-such); the heralds advertise other nonempty relations.
*** <localleader>la : :SkgShowFolderOfAliases
The aliasFolder -- other text you could search for to find this node
(you can always search for its title; most nodes have none). Writable:
type an alias in and save.
*** <localleader>lo : :SkgShowFolderOfOverrides
The overriddenFolder (the nodes this node overrides -- editable, shown
even when empty as an "add an override here" surface) and the
overriderFolder (the nodes that override this one -- write-protected, ☮).
*** <localleader>lh : :SkgShowFolderOfHidesFromSubs
The hiderFolder and hiddenFolder -- both write-protected (☮). Hiding is edited from
a subscribee-as-such, never from these folders. On a node that neither
hides nor is hidden, nothing appears.
*** <localleader>ls : :SkgShowFolderOfSubscribesTo
The subscribeeFolder (the nodes this node subscribes to -- editable, shown
even when empty) and the subscriberFolder (the nodes that subscribe to
this one -- write-protected, ☮).
*** <localleader>lp : :SkgShowFolderOfFlags
Shows the write-protected, true-only flags folder as titleless viewnodes whose
heralds carry their labels, in canonical order.
The empty folder is retained. Import provenance viewnodes have no setter; use the
search-matching command below for =No search matching=. Delete the whole
folder branch to dismiss this optional view without changing any flag.
*** <localleader>lc : :SkgShowFolderOfContainers
The containerFolder -- the nodes that contain this one. Write-protected (☮):
containment is edited from the container. Its other side, the node's
content, is shown without a folder. On a node nothing contains, nothing
appears.
*** <localleader>lm : :SkgShowFolderOfMentioners
The mentionerFolder -- the nodes that link to this one. Write-protected
(☮): a link lives in the linking node's text. On a node nothing links to,
nothing appears.
** <localleader>p : show a role tree (through one relation role)
Like the folders, each inserts a request that, on save, grafts the
partners reached through one relation role as inverted, write-protected
children, climbing transitively until a fork, cycle, or root. UPPER =
the partner's active (first) role; lower = its passive (second) role.
Every command auto-saves.
*** <localleader>pC : :SkgShowContainerwardTree
The nodes that contain this node (its containerward role tree).
*** <localleader>pL : :SkgShowMentionerwardTree
The nodes that link to this node (its mentioners).
*** <localleader>pl : :SkgShowMentionedwardTree
The nodes this node links to (the nodes it mentions).
*** <localleader>pO : :SkgShowOverriderwardTree
The nodes that override this node.
*** <localleader>po : :SkgShowOverriddenwardTree
The nodes this node overrides.
*** <localleader>pH : :SkgShowHiderwardTree
The nodes that hide this node from their subscriptions.
*** <localleader>ph : :SkgShowHiddenwardTree
The nodes this node hides from its subscriptions.
*** <localleader>pS : :SkgShowSubscriberwardTree
The nodes that subscribe to this node.
*** <localleader>ps : :SkgShowSubscribeewardTree
The nodes this node subscribes to.
** <localleader>s : setting node properties
*** first some vocab: 'editable' and 'write-protected'
A view of a node can be editable or write-protected.
Typically the first place in the buffer that depicts a node
is the editable view of it. So that other views of that node
cannot contradict it, they are 'write-protected': Edits to them
cannot affect the node they depict. One also has no content --
the server extends none under it,
in order to prevent the view from becoming redundant and huge --
but it may keep children that do not affect it.

A write-protected occurrence saves nothing of its own,
so an edit to it refuses the whole save, and nothing is written:
a changed title or home skgrepo;
an alias folder, partner folder or flags folder
that differs from the graph;
or a child that affects it (a member).
The refusal names the occurrence and what differs.
The way out is to make the edit at the node's editable occurrence
instead, or to undo it, make this occurrence editable
(<localleader>sd on it), save, and edit it then.
A child that should stay there can instead be marked
as not affecting its parent.
*** PITFALL: Don't make something 'editable' by directly editing its metadata.
Instead, use 'SetEditable' (<localleader>sd), below.
That's because Skg has to make other occurrences of it
(in this same buffer -- and maybe in the future other buffers too)
write-protected. That's because a buffer can only be saved
if it has at most one editable occurrence of a node.
Otherwise, two editable nodes could contradict each other.

Making a node write-protected is likewise a request
('RequestWriteProtected' (<localleader>sw), below), which the server
performs: it also makes the children of the write-protected occurrence
stop affecting it, since a write-protected occurrence has no content.
*** <localleader>sd : :SkgSetEditable
If you want to see the editable view of that node
from a place where it is currently shown in a write-protected form,
call this function. It will make the current editable view
(if it exists) write-protected, keeping what it shows
(though no longer as its content: each child that affected its parent
stops affecting it), and then make an editable view here.
Moving editability back to that occurrence later
makes those children its content again.
Called on a node that is already editable,
it extends the node's content editable,
up to 'initial_node_limit' extensions.
A buffer may carry only one such request per node.
It does not save; the request takes effect at the next save.
*** <localleader>sw : :SkgRequestWriteProtected
Requests that this occurrence become write-protected,
as described above. It does not save.
At the next save, edits the occurrence carries are saved first;
then the server makes it write-protected,
resyncing its title from the graph,
and makes each of its children stop affecting it,
so that edits to its title, body or children no longer affect it
  (although edits to its children still affect those children:
  they keep their own editability, and their own content).
On an occurrence that is already write-protected, it does nothing.
In one save with <localleader>sd on another occurrence of the same
node, it moves editability there.
The two requests on the same occurrence contradict each other,
and the save is refused.
*** <localleader>sW : :SkgRequestWriteProtectedRecursive
The same, for the occurrence and its whole content subtree:
every node in it becomes write-protected,
and every child under them stops affecting its parent.
*** <localleader>ss : :SkgSetRepo
Changes the skgrepo of the node at point.
The prompt starts with the current skgrepo as editable command-line
text. You can type the new skgrepo name directly,
or use S-Left / S-Right to cycle through owned skgrepos;
TAB completes among all configured skgrepo names.

The Emacs client's C-? helper (which opened an org buffer listing
every skgrepo from inside the minibuffer) has no cmdline analog --
few terminals deliver C-? reliably -- so it's dropped; run
':SkgViewRepoList' beforehand (or afterward) instead. It shows
the same thing: an org buffer listing every configured skgrepo name
as a headline, with that skgrepo's path as the headline body.

The command only edits the node's metadata in the current buffer.
Save the view afterward (':w') to apply the move.

A write-protected occurrence is not changed -- the save would
refuse its skgrepo edit -- and produces a loud WARNING,
with the full ID list in ':messages'.

What the move does to the relationships touching the moved nodes, the
save decides, whether or not the view shows them. One it would leave
more public than a node's new home (an inbound relationship of a move
to a more private skgrepo) is raised to that home, and the save's
warnings say so. If it would leave others at their old, more private
skgrepos, it saves nothing yet: it lists them and asks whether to
reset all of them to their new defaults, none, or each in turn;
then it saves with that answer, or not at all if you quit.
*** <localleader>sS : :SkgSetRepoRecursive
Like 'SetRepo', but it also
changes the skgrepo of every content descendent of the node at point
whose skgrepo matches the original skgrepo of the node at point.
Only descendents for which AffectsParent=True are traversed.
The write-protected warning and the save's handling of relationships
described under <localleader>ss apply here too, across the whole
subtree.
*** <localleader>sx : :SkgSetFlagSearchMatching
Prompts between =search matching= and =no search matching= and stages the
desired state without saving. Foreign/write-protected/unsaved roots and an
existing =editRequest= are refused.
*** <localleader>sX : :SkgSetFlagSearchMatchingRecursive
Applies one selected state uniformly through the true-content subtree,
deduplicating PIDs and reporting ineligible descendants. It prunes non-vognodes,
role trees, non-member branches, restricted nodes, and phantoms. Save with
=:w= afterward.
*** <localleader>sm : :SkgSetMergeRequest
(See [[./merging.org][the docs on merging]] for why would you merge two nodes,
and what it means to do that.)

Run this from the acquirer node.
It prompts for the acquiree, accepting either a bare ID
or an org link like =[[id:ID][label]]=,
and edits the acquirer's metadata to request a merge.

The command only edits the node's metadata in the current buffer.
Save the view afterward to apply the merge.
** <localleader>r : commit readiness, in the diff view
In a buffer of the diff view (<localleader>vd), each change can
be marked commit-ready. A mark approves the change as it is now:
editing the changed thing again makes the mark lapse. Marks live on
the server, in '<data_root>/readiness-marks.json'. A headline whose
change is ready shows ✓ after it; a commit readiness aggregate (a
folder of changes, a changeset marker) shows ✓ when all of its changes are. A node that
existed at HEAD and whose file records a change shows M ("modified"),
and M✓ once every change its file records is marked.

After every save of one of the diff view's buffers, a
notification shows the readiness summary: "12 of 14 changed files are
ready", or "Commit ready. All 14 of 14 changed files are ready.". A
changed file counts as ready when every change it records is marked;
a file whose only change is the order of a list counts as ready
without marks. The summary
adds how many changes are not editable in this view (<localleader>ru
integrates them) and how many files changed in foreign skgrepos.

A gesture that would unmark more than one change (a recursive one, one
on a folder of changes, or one on a modified node, which unmarks every
change the node records) first asks "Unmarking this node commit-ready
will unmark every contributing decision. You might discard a lot of
hard-won information. Continue (yes/no)?", and does nothing unless
you type "yes". Unmarking a single change asks nothing. The
server counts the changes: each headline that names changes says how
many, in its metadata's '(leaves N ...)'.
*** <localleader>rr : :SkgCycleCommitReady
Toggles the commit-readiness of the change at point, then saves.
On a headline that is one change (an old text, an alias, a move, a
changeset marker), it toggles that one. On a headline that carries
several, it toggles them all: on a new member its existence and its
relationship to the headline above it (∃ and ~); on a modified node
(M) every change its file records, and its relationship (~) when that
changed too, so one gesture marks the whole file. A headline counts
as ready when every one of its changes is. On a folder of changes, it
toggles each change one level down. Works on write-protected
headlines too.
*** <localleader>rR : :SkgCycleCommitReadyRecursive
Marks every change in the subtree at point, or unmarks them if the
headline at point is ready, then saves. (Emacs: C-u C-c r r.)
*** <localleader>rh : :SkgToggleHomeSkgrepoMoveCommitReady
Toggles the commit-readiness of the home-skgrepo move of the node at
point (or of the move at point), then saves: it unmarks the move if
it is ready, else marks it. Works on write-protected headlines too.
*** <localleader>rH : :SkgToggleHomeSkgrepoMoveCommitReadyRecursive
Also toggles, in the same direction, every descendant whose home
moved between the same two skgrepos. (Emacs: C-u C-c r h.)
*** <localleader>ru : :SkgDiffViewIntegrateUnshownChanges
Integrates every change not editable in the buffer of the diff view.
Each changed node with no editable occurrence becomes editable where
the buffer first shows it, in content or else in a partner folder,
with its change and its content shown under it; when a change is
under a root the buffer lacks, that root is appended at the end. A
notification then shows the readiness summary, as after a save.
Refuses with "Save the buffer first." while the buffer has unsaved
changes. (Emacs: C-c r u.)
*** <localleader>rc : :SkgStageAndCommit
Prompts once for a commit message, then stages every change and
git-commits it, in every owned skgrepo that has changes, with that
message. It stages only '.skg' files (deletions included). If not
every changed file is ready, it first shows the readiness summary and
proceeds only if you type the word "yes". Likewise, if some owned
gitrepo already has entries staged before the command, it first lists
each such gitrepo and its staged paths, and proceeds only on "yes";
the commit then includes those entries, since a git-commit records
everything staged. Every
open view must be saved or reverted first. Afterward the open buffers
of the diff view are rerendered: each keeps its roots, its
folding and what it made editable, and what was committed no longer
shows as a change. The
commit lapses the marks of everything it committed.
*** <localleader>rnc : :SkgDiffViewGotoNextChange
Moves the cursor to the next change headline after it: a headline
whose metadata carries a '(leaves ...)' fact, the server's count of
the changes it names. The cursor lands on the headline's metadata, as
with <localleader>in. It does not wrap: past the last one it says "No
further change" and leaves the cursor. It works in any skg buffer;
outside the diff view no headline names a change, so it finds none.
*** <localleader>rnu : :SkgDiffViewGotoNextUnreadyChange
The same, visiting only change headlines that are not ready (see
<localleader>rr for when a headline counts as ready). Past the last
one it says "No further unready change".
*** <localleader>rnr : :SkgDiffViewGotoNextReadyChange
The same, visiting only ready change headlines. Past the last one it
says "No further ready change".
*** <localleader>rpc : :SkgDiffViewGotoPreviousChange
Like <localleader>rnc, backward: moves the cursor to the previous
change headline before it. Before the first one it says "No earlier
change".
*** <localleader>rpu : :SkgDiffViewGotoPreviousUnreadyChange
Like <localleader>rnu, backward. Before the first one it says "No
earlier unready change".
*** <localleader>rpr : :SkgDiffViewGotoPreviousReadyChange
Like <localleader>rnr, backward. Before the first one it says "No
earlier ready change".
** <localleader>m : other graph modifications
*** <localleader>mc : :SkgReplaceLinkWithContent
Replace the leaf at point with a content relationship to the
node it links to, then save the buffer.

Point can be on the headline or in the node body. The node at
point can be new or already in the graph. If it already has an
ID, the command warns that the old node might become an orphan.

The headline title plus body must contain exactly one org bracket
link, and that link must be an =id:= link. The node must have no
viewdescendants. Its viewparent must be an editable unrestrictedNode
whose skgrepo is owned in =skgconfig.toml=.

The command replaces the whole leaf with a same-level
write-protected unrestrictedNode for the link target. The parent is
editable, so saving records the dest as content of the
parent; the replacement child is write-protected, so its own text is
not rewritten from the link label.
*** <localleader>mf : :SkgFork
Fork the node at point that you already own: create a private
clone that overrides it. This is the explicit counterpart to the
implicit fork (which is triggered by editing a /foreign/ node);
use it to deepen an override chain, e.g. to layer a private =D=
over a public clone =C= that already overrides a foreign =N=.

Refuses if the buffer has unsaved changes ("Save the buffer
before forking."), so the clone's saved state matches what you see.
Otherwise it stamps the node and auto-saves; the server returns
the usual fork-confirmation buffer (=skg://fork-confirmation=).
There you must set the clone's repo with 'SetRepo'
(<localleader>ss) (it starts as the placeholder PICK-A-REPO,
with your config-first owned skgrepo suggested above it), then
approve with <localleader>cc; or decline with <localleader>ck
(which also strips the fork request so the next save does not
re-fork). ':w' on the fork-confirmation buffer refuses and points
you back at these two keys.

The clone subscribes to and overrides the node, and the original
keeps its own (owned) content. A node may have at most one clone
you own; forking an already-forked node is rejected, naming the
existing clone. See =docs/forks.org=.
*** <localleader>ml : :SkgReplaceContentWithLink
Replace the branch at point with a link to the node that used to
be there, then save the buffer.

Point can be on the headline or in the node body.
The command uses the headline either way.

The node being replaced must be an existing unrestrictedNode with an ID,
and a viewchild of an editable unrestrictedNode whose skgrepo is
owned in =skgconfig.toml=. The command acts locally,
replacing only this occurrence in the current buffer:
the headline at point and all of its viewdescendants,
including non-vognodes and phantoms,
are removed from the view and replaced by a same-level headline
whose title is an =[[id:...][...]]= link to the original node.

If the original headline title already contains a link, the
command asks "Are you sure?" before proceeding.
** <localleader>v : view-level commands
*** <localleader>vd : :SkgDiffViewOpen
If you use git to manage your data,
this opens the diff view: every change in the owned skgrepos
since their last commits (how each worktree differs from HEAD), with
the context needed to understand it. It opens up to four buffers,
"skg://diff-view: all changes", "...: merges", "...: skgrepo changes"
and "...: order-only changes", skipping any that would be empty. It
refuses unless the skgrepo restriction is 'all', and when an owned
skgrepo is not in a git repository or has no HEAD commit (the refusal
names the skgrepo). A buffer keeps its roots until you close it, and
saving it (or committing) keeps what you folded. A save (of it or of
another view) decides what it adds anew by what changed: a new member
that changed, or leads to a change, is editable with its content, and
any other new member is a write-protected member shown without its
content. But a
save makes nothing editable that the buffer already shows, and
appends no root: the readiness summary counts a change since the
buffer opened that it holds nowhere editable as not editable in this
view. <localleader>ru integrates such changes.
Nothing the buffer holds editable is write-protected again by the
server. An editable-view
request (<localleader>sd) works as in any view, except that only the
extension of a node outside U (the nodes the buffer extends anyway:
those that changed and those leading to them) is charged to
'initial_node_limit'; nothing else in the buffer is bounded by that
limit.
Why the diff view commits whole skgrepos, and offers nothing
smaller: in skg a partial commit is dangerous. The graph is one
structure spread over many files, so committing some changed files
and not others leaves HEAD inconsistent: it can reference nodes it
does not contain, record a relationship from one end only, or hold a
moved node in two skgrepos at once. Such a HEAD cannot be reasoned
about, and the next diff view against it reports changes that are
only its own inconsistency. Review with the readiness marks
(<localleader>r) instead, and commit everything at once with
:SkgStageAndCommit.
The merges buffer shows each nodeMerge since HEAD: the acquiree and
its acquirer, in context. The acquiree's text preserver appears as a
new member of the acquirer's content. The skgrepo
changes buffer shows the nodes whose home skgrepo changed and the
nodes that record a relationship whose relRepo changed, each with all
of its changes; a moved node's
heralds read "-OLD +NEW", followed by "Δ⌂=a" when its nearest moved
ancestor (a, the viewparent; b, the grandparent; ...) moved the same
way. The order-only buffer lists the nodes whose only change is the
order of a list, each with its content in the new order.
*** <localleader>ve : :SkgViewNewEmpty
Asks you to pick a skgrepo,
and then provides a root node with that skgrepo.
**** why
Every node needs a skgrepo.
Children can inherit from their parents,
but to make a root (which has no parents)
you need to choose its skgrepo explicitly.
*** <localleader>vh : :SkgHeraldsToggle
This command toggles it.
This toggles whether, at the start of every node,
metadata is shown in its full plain-text glory,
or is instead summarized via brief 'heralds'.
It is turned on at every view by default.
See [[file:heralds.org][the herald legend]] for the tokens and styles.
*** <localleader>vL : :SkgToggleRepoOverlayOnLinks
Toggle display-only home skgrepo suffixes on Skg links in this buffer.
The suffixes start off. Links confirmed missing are ugly and underlined
even with suffixes off. See [[file:heralds.org::*Link annotations][link annotations]].
*** <localleader>vl : :SkgRestrictRepoSet
Restricts display and search to one configured skgrepo-set for this
Neovim connection.

The command asks which skgrepo-set to activate, with TAB completion
and S-Left / S-Right cycling. After confirmation it tells the server
to use that skgrepo-set and rerenders open Skg buffers in place. Choose
=all= to remove the restriction.

If the proposed set would rerender overPrivateText telescope text, Skg asks before
changing the skgrepo restriction or any view. Declining leaves both unchanged and
an empty rerender stream releases the client's preemptive locks.
*** <localleader>vm : :SkgViewMetadata
When called from a node in a view of the graph,
this switches to a view of the metadata of that node,
with one field per org branch. ':w' (or <localleader>cc) applies
the edited tree back into the source headline; ':bd!' cancels;
S-Left / S-Right cycle a field's value (writeProtected, affectsParent,
editRequest, skgrepo, ...).
It's easy to edit this way.
Note that some properties don't make sense to edit,
like the count of how many contents it has.
(If you want to change how much content a node has,
don't change the node's metadata; change its children in the view.)
*** <localleader>vo : :SkgViewAncestry
If you're at a headline so deep in the tree
that you can't remember where it came from,
this brings you to a new view showing only that ancestry.
This actually works in org-mode outside of skg.
(skg uses org-mode, but org-mode can be used without skg.)
*** <localleader>vr : :SkgReadableIdsToggle
This changes how node IDs are displayed.
The ID itself is a kind of special random gibberish called UUID v4.
When ReadableIdsToggle is on,
only the first 8 characters of the ID are shown (the rest is
concealed to an ellipsis, though the underlying text -- and
copy-paste -- still has the full ID),
and they are followed by the title of the node with that ID,
if Skg can figure it out. Works in .skg file buffers and in
git-status / git-diff buffers alike.
(It doesn't yet know how to read the git history
to find titles for deleted files.)
*** <localleader>vs : :SkgViewLinkstack
View and maybe edit the set of links you've stored.
(See "the linkstack" below.)
*** <localleader>vw : :SkgViewWithoutMetadata
If a Visual-mode selection is active (or was just left, via the
='<,'>= marks), opens a new org buffer containing that region,
but with the '(skg ...)' metadata stripped from every headline.
Otherwise it does nothing.
This is useful for copying a read-only projection of some data
into another application.
** <localleader>{i|u|o} : IDs, links and the linkstack
*** some background
**** IDs are mostly invisible, but good to know about.
Every node has an ID,
which you can see if you disable heralds ('HeraldsToggle',
<localleader>vh).
Every link also has an ID and a label,
but all you see when you look at the ID is the label,
unless you disable org-mode (say, by switching to text-mode).
You should never need to see IDs explicitly.
**** The linkstack
is, like it sounds, a stack of links.
A stack is just a list that you interact with,
mostly from one side, the 'top':
You can 'push' something onto the top of the stack,
and you can 'pop' something off of the top of the stack.
But you can also jump to a view of your entire stack,
using (copying, pasting, deleting) it
without any restrictions on order.
*** ]i (also <localleader>in) : :SkgIdNext
Makes the cursor hop among two kinds of IDs:
The ID associated with a node in the view,
and the ID associated with a link in a node's title.
Every node has an ID,
but a title can include multiple or no links.
*** [i (also <localleader>ip) : :SkgIdPrev
See IdNext, above.
*** the linkstack
<localleader>u for push, <localleader>o _ for paste,
<localleader>O _ for pop.

Inside a Vim command-line prompt (search, an Ex command's argument,
...), <localleader> chords aren't available, so paste and pop also
ride cmdline-mode mappings: <C-x>i pastes the top id, <C-x>l pastes
a link to it, <C-x>I pops the id, <C-x>L pops the link. (Push, and
pasting/popping a full node, have no cmdline form -- do those from
a buffer.)
**** <localleader>u : :SkgIdPush
Stores, in the linkstack,
a link to the node the cursor is on.
**** <localleader>oi : :SkgPasteId
Inserts the ID at the top of the linkstack at the cursor.
Does not modify the stack.
**** <localleader>Oi : :SkgPopId
Like PasteId,
but also removes the node from the stack.
**** <localleader>ol : :SkgPasteLink
Inserts, at the cursor, a link to the node
whose ID is at the top of the linkstack.
Does not modify the stack.
**** <localleader>Ol : :SkgPopLink
Like PasteLink,
but also removes the node from the stack.
**** <localleader>on : :SkgPasteNode
This is the easiest way to give a node multiple containers --
push it to the stack, then paste it as a node somewhere else.

Inserts, at the cursor, a write-protected view
of the node whose ID is at the top of the linkstack.
Its metadata includes only the ID, =writeProtected=,
and (usually) an editable view request;
its title comes from the stack.
Does not modify the stack or save.
Saving will provide the rest of its metadata,
and fulfill the editable view request,
making the node writable with its real title, body and content.

The view request is omitted if the buffer already has
an editable occurrence of the node (or one requesting an editable view),
because a buffer can hold only one editable occurrence of each node.
Then the pasted node stays write-protected, and Neovim says so.
**** <localleader>On : :SkgPopNode
Like PasteNode,
but also removes the node from the stack.
**** <localleader>vs : :SkgViewLinkstack
repeated here; described earlier in this doc
** buffer mechanics with no Emacs-chord counterpart
These are defined directly in =attach_content_view=
(nvim/lua/skg/keymaps.lua) rather than translated from a =C-c=
chord: they ride keys nvim already gives special meaning to.
*** <Tab> : toggle the fold at point
Equivalent to org's own =za=: opens or closes the fold under the
cursor.
*** <S-Tab> : toggle global fold visibility
All folds closed <-> all folds open, buffer-wide.
*** ^ : :SkgBeginningOfLine
Toggles the cursor between the start of the line and the start of
the title (the text after the stars and any =(skg ...)= metadata).
The nvim analog of the Emacs client's C-a toggle. On a
non-headline, it's just beginning-of-line.
*** cit / ciT : cycle the TODO keyword
Cycles the headline's TODO keyword forward (=cit=) or backward
(=ciT=) without corrupting its metadata: the =(skg ...)= sexp is
stripped before org's own TODO-cycling runs, then re-inserted
after the stars and before the (possibly new) keyword.
** importing Markdown and Org
*** :SkgImportMdAndOrg
With the server running, choose an absolute input directory in the
server/container filesystem and an existing owned destination skgrepo. The
skgrepo determines the privacy of all new nodes. Skg scans exact =.md= and
=.org= files recursively, leaves the originals untouched, and asks for a
host-root mapping only when absolute links to =.md= or =.org= files occur.
Blank mapping leaves unresolved links with warnings. Links to other kinds of
files are left pointing where they did, without warnings. Review the file/node counts, generated
export paths, and diagnostics; then explicitly confirm or decline. A changed
input or destination requires a fresh preview.

The import is additive: it creates file-root and headline nodes, an import
record, and an Org export marker under each file root. The import result
buffer links to the record; follow it with =<localleader>gg=. A document whose
only top-level headline has nothing before it uses that headline as its
file root. It does not replace
existing =.skg= files, copy attachments, synchronize later changes, or export
automatically. Most original markup remains text; Markdown hard breaks become
Org's two-backslash form so save-time trailing-whitespace cleanup remains.
Later export is a readable rendition, not a round-trip backup. Exporting to
the original directory overwrites matching =.org= files but not =.md= files.
There is no dedicated undo or crash-recovery transaction.

In Org files, link syntax inside text Org shows literally (=verbatim=,
~code~, a fixed-width line beginning with =: =, a =#+begin_...= block, or a
=```= fence) is an example, and is left alone; backticks are not literal in
Org. A line that looks like an Org headline inside a block or fence stops the
import, with nothing written; close the block, or escape the line with a
leading comma (=,* ...=). The Emacs command reference explains both in more
detail.

** exporting to org
*** :SkgExportToOrg
Exports Skg data to plain =.org= files, so the data can be read
(and navigated on GitHub) without running Skg. No keybinding.
Each file begins with comments naming its source node's ID and warning
that direct edits will be clobbered by the next export; the importer
ignores them.

It asks two things:
- which skgrepo-set to export (command-line input with TAB
  completion and S-Left / S-Right cycling); only nodes from that
  set are included. Choose a public-facing skgrepo-set so private
  notes are not exported; exporting =all= warns you about this.
- which directory to write to (default =org-exports=). This path
  is interpreted *by the server*, relative to the project root the
  server runs from. Because the server may run inside a Docker
  container whose filesystem differs from the host running Neovim,
  this prompt has no path completion. An absolute path is used
  as-is.

If a restricted export would include overPrivateText telescope text, Skg asks for
request-scoped approval before writing any file. Skgrepo-set =all= exports
it with a warning. The noninteractive form fails closed unless passed
=--include-overPrivateText-telescopes=:

: cargo run --bin skg -- export-org [config-path] [skgrepo-set] [output-dir] [--include-overPrivateText-telescopes]

A node is exported when one of its children's title links to the
export-instruction node and that child's body gives a
=target_filepath= (TOML-ish: =target_filepath = docs/setup=,
quoted if it contains whitespace). That parent is written to
=<output-dir>/<target_filepath>.org= as a recursive content view,
stripped of skg metadata. The marker child is omitted.

Links are rewritten to relative org links, except examples in text
Org shows literally (verbatim, code, fixed-width lines, blocks and
fences). A link to another
exported file's root points at that file; a link to a non-root
node points deep, via =[[./file.org::*Headline][label]]=, or via
=[[./file.org::#ID][label]]= when that headline contains a link
or repeats an earlier headline's text in its file
(the headline then gets a =:CUSTOM_ID: ID= property). A nested
export root is shown as a link, not inlined. A link whose dest
is not exported under the chosen set points to a "some links
might be broken" note.

Existing files in the output dir are overwritten in place; other
files there are left untouched.
** connection, reload, rebuild session-lifetime stores
Unless you're coding or troubleshooting,
you probably won't need these.
*** :SkgConnectionVerify
Sends a ping to the Rust server
to check if the connection is working.
Displays the result in the echo area.
*** :SkgConnectionEnd
Closes the TCP connection to the Rust server.
*** :SkgRebuildSessionLifetimeStores
Re-reads the authoritative =.skg= files, validates and replaces the in-memory
graph, and rebuilds the derived Tantivy search index. It does not rewrite the
=.skg= files.
Existing skg views are now invalid; run ':SkgCloseAllSkgBuffers'
to close them.
*** :SkgCloseAllSkgBuffers
This may be warranted after an session-lifetime-store rebuild.
Kills every skg view buffer (each triggers a close-view notice to
the server first).
*** :SkgReload
Unloads all skg Lua modules and reloads them from disk.
Useful when you've changed Lua code
and want to pick up the changes without restarting Neovim.
